name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain = chapter_29, descriptor = post_action. The '29' is the chapter ID (game domain, valid range 01-30), NOT a Ghidra address residue: confirmed dispatched as data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table[28] @ 0x51B89 (table base 0x51B19 + 28*4), and the handler table is indexed by current_chapter_id with chapter N at index N-1, so index 28 -> chapter 29. The descriptor accurately reflects the function (per-chapter turn-cycle post-action win/lose handler). No hex-address fragment in the name.
purpose: Chapter 29 turn-cycle post-action win/lose handler. Map-event driven: wins when 3 altar/event tiles are all triggered, loses if either of the two protected chars (hero slot 0, ally slot 1) dies (the ally death also shows a chapter dialog page).
logic_summary: Does NOT call the default fd2_check_battle_end_condition. Three sequential independent writes to data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0x53ECC), later writes overriding earlier: (1) WIN - load data_fd2_field_map_tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr (0x53AD5); if bytes [0x12], [0x13], [0x14] are ALL nonzero (3 altars/locations triggered), set code = 2; the && short-circuits on the first un-triggered tile. (2) LOSE - if fd2_check_char_is_dead(0) (hero), set code = 1; runs after step 1 so a hero death overrides a WIN. (3) LOSE+dialog - if fd2_check_char_is_dead(1) (ally), call fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page=9, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1) then set code = 1.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch-table function-pointer arg slot; unused by the body. The decompiler surfaces it only because the Watcom __CHK stack-probe prologue (PUSH 0x28 / CALL 0x36CD7) is mis-modeled as a param push. The dispatch site invokes the handler with no real argument; src explicitly (void)event_arg.
params.reason: Name is accurate and address-residue-free: 'event_arg' documents that this is the (unused) dispatch event-arg slot, and it matches the consistent convention used by all sibling post-action handlers in chpost.c. Renaming would diverge from that convention and force a Stage 2 change to the shared dispatch-table type for no semantic gain.

returns.semantics: No return value. Effect is communicated via the global data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0x53ECC): 0=continue, 1=LOSE/game over, 2=WIN/chapter switch.

notes: Verified against disasm @ 0x20B72: PUSH 0x28 / CALL 0x36CD7 (__CHK stack-probe, frame=0x28; the decompile 'event_arg' + in_stack_* vars are __CHK artifacts, not real params -- body uses no argument). MOV EAX,[0x53AD5]=data_fd2_field_map_tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr; CMP byte [EAX+0x12/0x13/0x14],0 all-nonzero -> MOV dword [0x53ECC],2 (WIN). CALL 0x3453E (fd2_check_char_is_dead) arg 0, TEST EAX -> [0x53ECC]=1 (LOSE). CALL 0x3453E arg 1, then CALL 0x15F84 (fd2_display_dialog_scene) with [0x53A79]=data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page 9, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1; then [0x53ECC]=1 (LOSE). Write order WIN(step1) then LOSE(step2) then LOSE+dialog(step3) -> lose-overrides-win (matches chapter 30 pattern, inverse of chapters 18/23). Dispatch confirmed: handler-table[28] @ 0x51B89 = 0x20B72. Callees verified by name: 0x3453E=fd2_check_char_is_dead, 0x15F84=fd2_display_dialog_scene, 0x36CD7=__CHK. All three globals declared in src/include/globals.h and used consistently across the codebase. Existing src comment (chpost.c lines 549-579) already precisely matches verified logic incl. ordering/override semantics and the __CHK-artifact note -> comment_verdict=keep, no src edit. Ghidra plate consistent (same 3-way logic, same addresses, same WIN/LOSE codes), not contradictory/outdated -> plate left unchanged.
